title: From droplet to raindrop
summary: Cloud droplets are far too small to fall. This is how they grow heavy enough to reach the ground, and what shape they are when they do.

blocks.text: Rain is one kind of [[precipitation]]: water released from clouds as rain, freezing rain, sleet, snow or hail.
The droplets in a cloud are far too small to fall as rain. To reach the ground, they have to grow.
Droplets bump into each other and join together, which is called [[coalescence]]. Millions of cloud droplets are needed to make a single raindrop.
A drop leaves the cloud once it falls faster than the [[updraft]], the rising air inside the cloud.
When a cloud holds ice crystals, the crystals can grow quickly by taking water from the cloud. This is called the [[Bergeron process]].
The crystals may fall as snow, or melt on the way down and fall as rain.
Raindrops are not shaped like teardrops. Small drops, with a radius under 1 millimetre, are round like a ball.

items: At about 2 to 3 millimetres across, a falling drop is flat underneath, like a hamburger bun.
At about 4 to 5 millimetres, the dip in its bottom grows into a shape like a parachute.
Bigger still, the drop breaks up into smaller drops.

blocks.alt: Four drawings from left to right: a small round drop, a wider drop flattened underneath, a large drop hollowed out like a parachute, and a cluster of small drops after it splits.
blocks.caption: As a falling drop grows, air pushes its bottom flat, then hollows it out, until it splits.

takeaways: Cloud droplets must grow before they can fall.
They grow by merging, and in icy clouds by the Bergeron process.
Small raindrops are round; bigger ones flatten, hollow out and split.
recap: Cloud droplets are too small to fall, so they have to grow.
They merge, and millions of them make one raindrop.
In icy clouds, crystals grow fast and fall as snow, or melt into rain.
Small raindrops are round, and big ones flatten and break apart.

quiz.question: Roughly how many cloud droplets does one raindrop take?
quiz.proof: Millions of cloud droplets are needed to make a single raindrop.

options: When it falls faster than the updraft
